android.head: App Total Revenue -5.2% does not match new subs +3.4% from 7 days earlier — this drop is not coming from new customers.
android.body: App Total Revenue on 10-30 vs 10-23 is -5.2%, but App Total New Subs on 10-23 vs 10-16 was +3.4% — they did not move together. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the subscription revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. By purchase type (on 10-30 vs 10-23): Subscription -9.7%, Pay as you go +81.9%. Since new subs moved the other way while Subscription revenue (-9.7%) did not follow them, this drop is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

android.head: Subscription revenue is down 21.1%; Pay as you go +187.6% is softening it (total -15.4%).
android.body: App Total Revenue (YMK · US) was 2,438, against 2,881 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks (-442). By purchase type: Subscription -592 (-21.1%), Pay as you go +149 (+187.6%). Pay as you go is 9.4% of revenue. The recurring part is what new subs feed, so the Pay as you go lift is one-off cover, not a recovery.

android.head: Pay as you go is a bigger part of revenue than usual (9.4% vs 2.8%).
android.body: Pay as you go (YMK · US) is 9.4% of revenue, versus 2.8% for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks. More of the money is one-off spend rather than recurring subscriptions.

android.head: Where installs come from is shifting toward Paid Install (+7.0% vs -47.2% for installs overall).
android.body: Paid Install (YMK · US) was 591, +7.0% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -47.2% — a difference of +54.2 percentage points. Paid Install is now 100.0% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving toward it.

android.head: App Total New User is moving faster than the other steps (+8.0% vs about -39.7%).
android.body: App Total New User is +8.0% while the other steps are all moving about -39.7% — a gap of +47.7pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

android.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
android.body: App Total New Subs is -39.7% and App Total Install is -47.2%; the gap between them (+7.5pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.

ios.head: App Total New User is moving slower than the other steps (+42.0% vs about +50.0%).
ios.body: App Total New User is +42.0% while the other steps are all moving about +50.0% — a gap of -8.0pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

ios.head: App Total Install +58.0% — Organic Install is behind most of it (+1,195, +107.4%).
ios.body: App Total Install (YMK · US) was 5,715, against 3,618 for the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks — a change of +2,097. Where that came from: Organic Install +1,195 (+107.4%), Paid Install +913 (+39.5%), SEO Install +22 (+28.6%). Organic Install moved the most on its own (+1,195, +107.4%) and is now 40.4% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

insights.title: Which app — App Total Install -6.0% is mostly YCP — not every app.
insights.body: App Total Install moved -6.0% overall, but the apps are far apart (All App -6.0%, YMK +33.9%, YCP -94.7%, YCV +8.0%, YCE +6.9%, YCA +11.7%). YCP accounts for most of it, so look at what changed in that one app rather than something affecting all of them.

insights.title: Install mix — Where installs come from is shifting away from SEO Install (-15.8% vs -6.0% for installs overall).
insights.body: SEO Install was 1,498, -15.8% against the average of the same weekday over the past 4 weeks, while total installs moved -6.0% — a difference of -9.8 percentage points. SEO Install is now 5.9% of all installs, so the balance between channels is moving away from it; free traffic slipping while paid holds up means we are buying more of the same installs..
